standard_prerequisites: The calculus G3c and the notion of height-preserving admissibility.
Height-preserving invertibility of the G3c rules (the inversion lemma), used when the contracted formula is principal in the last inference.

Height-preserving invertibility of the quantifier rules in the fresh-constant sense, and the regularity and substitution machinery for replacing a fresh constant by an arbitrary term without changing proof height.
core_obligations: Prove that both contraction rules are height-preserving admissible in G3c by induction on the proof height, with the inductive hypothesis stated for arbitrary contexts and arbitrary contracted formula.
Non-principal case: apply the inductive hypothesis to the immediate subproofs and re-apply the last rule, exemplified in full for right-and.

Principal case for a propositional principal formula: invert the immediate subproofs height-preservingly, contract in each by the inductive hypothesis, and re-apply the rule, exemplified for right-and.

Principal quantifier cases: for the universal right case, invert with a fresh constant, regularize, substitute the eigenvariable by a constant not occurring elsewhere via the substitution lemma, apply the inductive hypothesis, and re-apply the universal right rule checking the eigenvariable condition; for the existential right case, the inductive hypothesis alone suffices and no inversion is needed.
proof_roadmap: Set the induction with the strengthened hypothesis and dispatch the height-zero case by atomicity of G3c axioms.
Dispatch the non-principal case generically with the right-and instance.
Dispatch the propositional principal case through the inversion lemma with the right-and instance.

Dispatch the two quantifier-principal cases, the universal one through fresh-constant inversion plus substitution plus the inductive hypothesis, the existential one through the inductive hypothesis alone, verifying the eigenvariable side conditions.
difficulty_reason: A four-case analysis where the quantifier-principal branch chains fresh-constant inversion, regularity, and substitution before the inductive hypothesis applies; the substantive steps are the strengthened inductive hypothesis and the eigenvariable bookkeeping in the substitution step.
